features.name: Writing polish
features.description: This captures the surface professionalism of the letter's spelling, grammar, and copy accuracy.

levels.descriptor: Frequent errors, misspellings, or naming mistakes noticeably distract from the application.
Several noticeable errors appear, but the letter remains readable.
Mostly clean writing with only minor slips.
Polished, professional, and essentially error-free throughout.

features.name: impact articulation
features.description: Captures how clearly the letter states the effect of the applicant's work on capacity, reliability, or security outcomes.

levels.descriptor: Lists duties or technologies without describing resulting impact.
Claims improvement in general terms, but without a concrete effect.
States a clear operational effect, such as reduced manual work, better routing, or improved reliability.
Quantifies the outcome or conveys it vividly enough that the scale of benefit is easy to grasp.

features.name: impact specificity
features.description: Captures whether accomplishments are supported with concrete operational detail, outcomes, or measurement rather than broad assertions.

levels.descriptor: Relies mostly on abstract claims about skill or fit.
Names responsibilities or technologies, but gives little outcome detail.
Provides concrete examples of work with clear scope or implied benefit.
Provides concrete accomplishments with explicit operational impact, measurement, or before-and-after improvement.

features.name: Specificity of evidence
features.description: This captures how much the letter backs claims with concrete mechanisms, examples, or outcomes instead of generic assertions.

levels.descriptor: Relies mostly on generic claims or alignment statements.
Provides some concrete terms or examples but not enough to let the reader picture the work.
Uses several specific examples, mechanisms, or outcomes to support claims.
Is densely grounded in concrete evidence, with enough operational detail that the work feels tangible and credible.

features.name: Voice
features.description: This captures whether the letter has a distinctive professional voice and memorable framing rather than sounding purely formulaic.

levels.descriptor: Reads as flat, compliance-style prose with little individuality.
Reads as competent but familiar and interchangeable with many other applications.
Shows a clear personal voice or a strong framing device that adds interest.
Sustains a memorable, controlled voice that makes the letter stand out beyond its credential list.

features.name: opening framing
features.description: This captures whether the letter opens with a distinctive, role-relevant idea that makes the applicant memorable beyond a generic application statement.

levels.descriptor: Opens generically, with little role-specific framing or memorable point of view.
States interest clearly but in a conventional way that does not add much distinctiveness.
Uses a specific, role-relevant framing idea that helps the reader remember the application.
Opens with a striking, insightful framing that sharpens both motivation and fit.

features.name: Narrative distinctiveness
features.description: Captures how memorable and cohesive the letter's voice and overall story are beyond a checklist of qualifications.

levels.descriptor: Reads as transactional or template-like, with little memorable voice.
Clear and competent but conventional.
Has a noticeable voice or coherent personal arc that helps the reader remember the candidate.
Uses distinctive framing and a well-integrated story that actively strengthens the case for fit.

features.name: academic credential
features.description: This captures the highest formal academic preparation the letter presents in a relevant technical field.

levels.descriptor: Bachelor's degree, equivalent, or no advanced degree is presented.
Master's degree is presented.
Doctoral degree is presented.

features.name: Academic qualification signal
features.description: Captures how strong the formal educational credential is relative to the role's minimum and preferred qualifications.

levels.descriptor: No degree or equivalent preparation is made clear.
Shows a bachelor's degree or equivalent practical background.
Shows a master's degree or comparable advanced study.
Shows a doctorate or similarly strong advanced academic credential.

features.name: AI production maturity
features.description: This captures whether the applicant has hands-on AI experience and whether they frame it in terms of reliable production deployment rather than novelty.

levels.descriptor: No AI experience is mentioned.
Mentions AI or LLM exposure without concrete deployment detail.
Describes shipped AI features or workflows in production.
Describes shipped AI work plus evaluation, hardening, guardrails, or trustworthiness practices.

features.name: Go track record
features.description: This captures the strength of direct Go experience in production backend work.

levels.descriptor: Mentions Go but does not make its role in shipped work clear.
Shows regular working use of Go that plausibly meets the role requirement.
Presents Go as a primary language across multiple production services.
Shows substantial long-term Go ownership in building and operating backend systems.

features.name: Production systems track record
features.description: Captures the breadth of concrete production-service experience described, especially launch and maintenance of real systems.

levels.descriptor: Mentions only limited production exposure or one to two services.
Describes several production systems, typically three to four, or moderate ownership across launch and maintenance.
Shows broad production experience, such as five or more services and or clear end-to-end responsibility.

features.name: professional tenure
features.description: Captures the amount of post-school software engineering experience the letter claims.

levels.descriptor: Roughly entry-to-early career tenure, around 2 to 3 years, or unclear total experience.
Solid mid-level tenure, around 4 to 5 years.
Seasoned tenure, around 6 or more years.

features.name: Production delivery breadth
features.description: This captures how much shipped-service experience the letter claims, using number of production services as a proxy for exposure to launch and maintenance cycles.

levels.descriptor: Describes launching or owning only a small number of production services, such as 2.
Describes a moderate shipped footprint, such as about 4 production services.
Describes repeated launch and maintenance experience across many services, such as 6 or more.

features.name: Shipped service breadth
features.description: Captures the breadth of hands-on experience across testing, maintaining, and launching production services.

levels.descriptor: No clear evidence of owning production services through launch and maintenance.
Shows limited shipped-service exposure, such as one or two services or mostly maintenance work.
Shows solid multi-service exposure across the production lifecycle.
Shows repeated ownership across many production services with clear launch and upkeep experience.

features.name: Production engineering scope
features.description: Captures the breadth of professional software delivery experience the letter demonstrates through years of work, maintenance history, and production launch ownership.

levels.descriptor: Experience is unclear, below the minimum, or lacks evidence of real production responsibility.
Meets the baseline with a few years of experience and limited examples of launched or maintained production systems.
Shows solid mid-level scope with several years of experience and multiple production services.
Shows strong scope with repeated launch, maintenance, and testing responsibility across several services over many years.
Shows especially broad production depth through long tenure plus high service count or unusually strong evidence of sustained ownership.

features.name: production software track record
features.description: This captures how much concrete professional experience the letter presents in testing, maintaining, and launching production software, including breadth of shipped systems.

levels.descriptor: Meets the baseline only, with limited scope or a small number of launched systems described.
Shows a solid early-career record, with several years and some repeated launch or maintenance work.
Shows a strong mid-career record, with multiple launches and clear production breadth.
Presents an extensive record for this role, combining years, repeated launches, and broad responsibility across production systems.

features.name: delivery volume
features.description: Captures how many distinct production services the applicant says they have tested, maintained, or launched.

levels.descriptor: Only 1 to 2 production services are cited, or shipped-system breadth is unclear.
About 3 to 4 production services are cited.
5 or more production services are cited, signaling broader delivery exposure.

features.name: Algorithmic problem-solving
features.description: Captures whether the letter demonstrates real fluency with data structures and algorithms through concrete engineering examples.

levels.descriptor: No algorithmic strength is mentioned.
Claims strong data-structure or algorithm knowledge, but without a concrete example.
Gives at least one concrete example of improving a system through better algorithm or data-structure choice.
Uses a specific, nontrivial example to show strong algorithmic judgment and a meaningful systems improvement.

features.name: Python depth
features.description: This captures the depth and seriousness of the applicant's Python use, especially for production services, tooling, or automation.

levels.descriptor: Python is absent or only minimally mentioned.
Python is mentioned for light scripting or general familiarity.
Python is used regularly for tooling, automation, analysis, or services.
Python is presented as production-grade and central, with evidence of robust service or tooling development.

features.name: Python production fluency
features.description: Captures how clearly the letter shows Python as a serious working language for services, automation, or tooling relevant to the role.

levels.descriptor: No meaningful Python experience is mentioned.
Python is mentioned mainly for scripts or light tooling.
Python is shown as a regular production language for services, tooling, or automation.
Python is presented as production-grade or central to important internal systems and automation.

features.name: Language breadth
features.description: This captures the range of additional programming languages the applicant claims beyond Go.

levels.descriptor: No additional languages are mentioned.
Mentions 1 to 2 additional languages.
Mentions 3 to 5 additional languages.
Mentions more than 5 additional languages.

features.name: Go backend depth
features.description: Captures how central Go is to the applicant's production engineering experience.

levels.descriptor: Go is absent or its use is unclear.
Go is mentioned, but the depth of use is limited or generic.
Go is clearly a primary language used on production services or back-end systems.
Go is presented as central to back-end architecture, especially in systems relevant to security tooling, platform work, or agent control.

features.name: Go centrality
features.description: This captures how strongly the letter presents Go as a primary working language rather than a box-checking mention.

levels.descriptor: Go is absent or its use is unclear.
Go is mentioned, but not as a major language in the applicant's work.
Go is presented as a regular or important language for backend work.
Go is clearly described as a primary language or daily driver tied to substantial backend ownership.

features.name: Go fluency signal
features.description: This captures how strongly the letter positions Go as a central professional language rather than a peripheral one.

levels.descriptor: Go is mentioned only briefly, or the depth of use is unclear.
Go is clearly used in professional work, but it is not framed as the applicant's main language.
Go is framed as a primary, daily, or chief working language in meaningful production context.

features.name: agentic systems ownership
features.description: This captures experience designing agentic tooling, especially architectures that give agents bounded autonomy under supervised infrastructure.

levels.descriptor: No agentic systems experience is mentioned.
References agents in passing without clear ownership or design detail.
Describes a concrete agentic pipeline or tooling example.
Shows end-to-end ownership of agentic architecture, including boundaries, supervision, permissions, logging, or auditability.

features.name: Personal project ambition
features.description: Captures the technical ambition of self-directed projects described outside the applicant's day job.

levels.descriptor: No personal project is mentioned.
Mentions a small utility or light side project with modest technical scope.
Describes a substantive side project with meaningful systems or infrastructure work.
Describes an ambitious self-directed systems project tackling distributed correctness, recovery, delivery guarantees, or similarly hard engineering problems.

features.name: Open-source stewardship
features.description: This captures the degree to which the letter shows external code contribution, maintenance, or responsibility to users beyond the applicant's employer.

levels.descriptor: No open-source activity is mentioned.
Mentions occasional patches or minor contributions.
Shows regular contributions or maintainership of a small project.
Maintains a project with outside users or community responsibilities such as reviews, releases, issue handling, or roadmap decisions.

features.name: CTF engagement
features.description: This captures whether the letter shows active offensive-security practice through capture-the-flag competition.

levels.descriptor: Shows no capture-the-flag or similar competitive offensive practice.
Mentions occasional or casual participation.
Shows regular and serious participation.
Shows strong competitive results such as near-top finishes in substantial fields.

features.name: Offensive security practice
features.description: This captures the extent to which the letter shows ongoing adversarial practice through CTFs or similar attacker-oriented work.

levels.descriptor: No offensive-practice evidence is mentioned.
Mentions casual or occasional participation with little detail.
Shows regular participation presented as deliberate skill maintenance.
Shows strong results or serious competitive commitment that signals sustained offensive practice.

features.name: Security assessment practice
features.description: Captures how directly the letter shows hands-on security review work such as threat modeling, attack-surface analysis, code review, or remediation validation.

levels.descriptor: No assessment experience is shown.
Shows only general security interest or vocabulary without direct assessment work.
Shows direct experience performing security reviews or assessments.
Shows direct assessment experience plus method detail, such as threat models, attacker mindset, attack-surface mapping, or remediation verification.

features.name: Security credential strength
features.description: This captures the rigor of the formal security credentialing the letter offers as external validation.

levels.descriptor: No relevant security certification is stated.
A baseline or survey credential such as Security+ is stated.
A rigorous hands-on credential such as OSCP or a similarly demanding practical certification is stated.

features.name: vulnerability triage automation
features.description: This captures direct experience automating the intake, classification, routing, or deduplication of vulnerability reports.

levels.descriptor: No vulnerability-handling automation is described.
Shows general automation interest, but not with a concrete vulnerability triage example.
Describes a clear example of automating vulnerability intake or routing.
Describes a strong triage automation example with several functions such as classification, deduplication, prioritization, routing, or measurable manual-load reduction.

features.name: Platform security mission fit
features.description: This captures how directly the letter aligns the applicant's motivation with secure-by-default, organization-wide security enablement.

levels.descriptor: Motivation is generic or could apply to almost any software role.
Shows general interest in backend work, infrastructure, or security impact.
Clearly values secure defaults, foundational leverage, or helping developers do the right thing by default.
Frames the work as scaling scarce security expertise across the development lifecycle and shows strong philosophical alignment with that mission.

features.name: Role-specific motivation
features.description: Captures how clearly the letter explains why this exact security engineering role is appealing rather than a generic software job.

levels.descriptor: Shows generic interest in the company or job title with little role-specific reasoning.
Shows some relevant interest, but the motivation remains broad or interchangeable.
Clearly ties motivation to security engineering, developer enablement, or backend tooling.
Gives nuanced and convincing motivation tightly tied to this team's charter and responsibilities.

features.name: Role-specific security workflow insight
features.description: Captures how specifically the letter engages with this team's actual work, such as vulnerability handling, variant analysis, AI agents, or Google Core scale.

levels.descriptor: Expresses generic interest in security engineering with no role-specific details.
Echoes broad job themes like security impact or automation, but without concrete workflow understanding.
Engages at least one specific responsibility, such as vulnerability triage, AI agents, or foundational internal tooling.
Shows nuanced understanding of multiple role-specific problems and why they matter together.

features.name: security automation framing
features.description: Captures how well the letter articulates the core problem of scaling security work through tooling rather than describing the role only at a surface level.

levels.descriptor: Shows little role-specific framing beyond wanting security impact.
Shows general interest in secure defaults or automation, but not a sharp view of the problem.
Clearly frames security tooling as a way to scale review, response, or manual workload.
Frames the problem sharply in terms of scarce expert attention, organization-wide signal handling, variant analysis, or systems-level leverage.

features.name: Engineering rigor
features.description: Captures emphasis on correctness, guardrails, maintainability, testing, and dependable operation in security-related software.

levels.descriptor: Provides little evidence of maintainability, testing, safety, or operational care.
Shows some signals of care, such as a maintainer mindset or concern for correctness, but not many concrete practices.
Names explicit rigor practices such as testing, typing, bounded actions, release discipline, or failure recovery.
Repeatedly signals high production standards and a habit of building dependable systems with strong constraints and maintainability.

features.name: Security rigor philosophy
features.description: Captures whether the letter articulates a principled view of security engineering as unusually high-standard, dependable work.

levels.descriptor: Offers no distinct philosophy about the quality bar required for security engineering.
Makes only generic statements about reliability or security importance.
Expresses a clear philosophy of quiet resilience, dependable systems, or a higher standard for security tooling.
Builds a memorable, well-integrated case that security tooling demands exceptional rigor and ties that belief to prior work or design choices.

features.name: Security-partner orientation
features.description: Captures whether the letter presents the candidate as ready to collaborate closely with security specialists rather than operating in isolation.

levels.descriptor: Does not mention collaboration with security partners.
Implies support for other engineers, but not specifically partnership with security specialists.
Explicitly states readiness to work with security engineers or build for their workflows.
Shows explicit partnership mindset plus concrete evidence of learning from, serving, or collaborating with security specialists.

features.name: Developer enablement mindset
features.description: Captures whether the letter frames security tooling as something that helps developer teams adopt safer defaults with less friction.

levels.descriptor: Does not discuss the needs or behavior of developer users.
Mentions helping teams in generic terms.
Explicitly focuses on reducing friction or making the secure path easier for developers.
Shows clear empathy for busy engineers and explains adoption in terms of defaults, workflows, and usable tooling rather than process.

features.name: Secure-defaults motivation
features.description: This captures how specifically the applicant connects their interest in the role to making security easier and more natural for developers.

levels.descriptor: The letter shows only generic interest in the company or title.
The letter shows general security interest but does not tie it to developer workflows or defaults.
The letter clearly connects the role to embedding security in the development lifecycle or reducing manual security toil.
The letter articulates a strong philosophy of secure defaults, proactive developer enablement, or higher engineering standards for security tooling.

features.name: Platform leverage orientation
features.description: Captures whether the applicant is motivated by central infrastructure work whose benefits compound across many teams.

levels.descriptor: Does not show any particular interest in foundational or shared systems work.
Mentions scale or impact in passing, but not as a central motivation.
Explicitly values platform or infrastructure work because it benefits many teams.
Persuasively frames central tooling as a multiplier, emphasizing inherited impact or organization-wide capacity gains.

features.name: platform leverage mindset
features.description: Captures whether the applicant frames impact in terms of central systems that multiply security gains across many teams.

levels.descriptor: Shows no platform-scale framing.
Mentions scale in a generic way, mostly as company size or reach.
Explicitly values foundational, central, or infrastructure work that benefits many teams.
Clearly explains multiplier effects such as secure defaults, capacity gains, downstream leverage, or fleet-wide protection.

features.name: Maintainability mindset
features.description: Captures whether the letter explicitly values reliability, inheritance, and long-term operability of the systems it builds.

levels.descriptor: Shows no explicit maintainability or reliability orientation.
Implies care for quality but not as a recurring theme.
Clearly values maintainable, dependable systems or draws on maintenance experience.
Makes long-term operability a central lens, emphasizing inheritance, quiet resilience, or higher standards for security-critical software.

features.name: Upstream repair habit
features.description: Captures whether the letter shows a habit of fixing defects in dependencies or tools at the source instead of only working around them locally.

levels.descriptor: No evidence of upstream fixing appears.
Mentions occasional or general upstream contributions.
Shows a clear recurring habit of writing and shepherding patches to source projects.
